name: L1e-B Moped
description: A two-wheeler of no more than 4 kW that can't go faster than 45 km/h and isn't an L1e-A powered cycle, such as a speed pedelec assisting past 25 km/h: an L1e-B moped under the UK's assimilated copy of Regulation (EU) No 168/2013. It must be approved, registered, taxed and insured, and its rider needs a category AM licence, or CBT and L plates on a provisional one, and a motorcycle helmet.

restrictions.rule: Two wheels, a maximum design speed of no more than 45 km/h, and a maximum continuous rated or net power of no more than 4,000 W
Past the L1e-A limits, assisting beyond 25 km/h or with more than 1,000 W; one within them is an L1e-A powered cycle instead
A motor vehicle, so one first used from January 2016 must be type approved, or get a Motorcycle Single Vehicle Approval as a two-wheeled moped, before it can be registered
restrictions.citation: Road Traffic Act 1988, s. 189(1)(c); Regulation (EU) No 168/2013 (assimilated), art. 2(1)

restrictions.rule: Must be registered with the DVLA and taxed, at the zero-emission motorcycle rate
Must be insured for use on a road or other public place; an uninsured one may be seized
A moped for licensing, so the rider needs a category AM licence from age 16, earned with CBT, a theory test and a practical test; a full A or car (B) licence includes AM
restrictions.citation: Road Traffic Act 1988, ss. 87, 108(1); Directive 2006/126/EC (assimilated), art. 4(2); Motor Vehicles (Driving Licences) Regulations 1999, SI 1999/2864, reg. 9(1A), Sch. 2

restrictions.rule: On a provisional licence, the rider must first complete compulsory basic training (CBT), display L plates (D plates allowed in Wales) and carry no passenger
restrictions.citation: Road Traffic Act 1988, s. 97(3)(e); Motor Vehicles (Driving Licences) Regulations 1999, SI 1999/2864, reg. 16

restrictions.rule: The rider and any passenger must wear a motorcycle helmet meeting BS 6658:1985 or UNECE Regulation 22.05 or 22.06, unless a Sikh wearing a turban
restrictions.citation: Motor Cycles (Protective Helmets) Regulations 1998, SI 1998/1807, reg. 4; Road Traffic Act 1988, s. 16(2)

restrictions.rule: Needs an MOT test certificate once it's three years past first registration
Ridden only on the road: not on cycle tracks, cycle lanes or pavements
restrictions.citation: Road Traffic Act 1988, s. 21; Roads (Scotland) Act 1984, s. 129(5)

restrictions.rule: In Northern Ireland too it's a motorcycle or moped: it must be type approved, registered, taxed and insured, and its rider needs a driving licence and a motorcycle helmet
